title: useUIStore() subscribed without a selector forces App to re-render on every UI-store mutation
description: The hook calls `const { setShortcutsOpen, setSubmodelDialog, setNodeSearchOpen } = useUIStore()` with no selector, subscribing the consuming component (App, the top-level component) to the entire UI store. Any UI-store change (hoveredNodeId, paletteOpen, nodePanelWidth, explorePanes, etc.) re-renders App even though this hook only ever needs three referentially-stable setters. The file is inconsistent with itself one line up — line 32 uses a selector (`useToastStore((s) => s.addToast)`). Because the setters are stable Zustand actions, a selector (or `useUIStore.getState()` inline, mirroring how the hook already reads `useUIStore.getState().nodeSearchOpen` at line 136) avoids the spurious subscription with no behavior change.
evidence: Line 33: `const { setShortcutsOpen, setSubmodelDialog, setNodeSearchOpen } = useUIStore()`. Store (useUIStore.ts:62) defines actions once in `create((set) => ({...}))` so they are stable; the no-selector subscription only adds re-renders. Line 32 already demonstrates the selector idiom; line 136 already uses `useUIStore.getState()` for one-off reads.
est_reduction: ~1 line changed; removes whole-store subscription on the top-level App component
behavior_preservation: Setters are stable store actions; reading them via a selector or getState yields identical references and identical handler behavior, only reducing re-render frequency.
